items.title: Block Inc. reaches settlement in principle for $442.5 million in federal securities class action
items.summary: Block Inc. agreed in principle to settle a federal securities class action for approximately $442.5 million. The lawsuit, filed in January 2025, alleged violations of securities laws by the company and certain officers related to Class A common stock purchased between February 26, 2020 and August 1, 2024. The settlement is subject to preliminary and final court approval.

items.title: Carnival Corp amends CEO Josh Weinstein's restricted stock unit grant
items.summary: Carnival Corporation's Compensation Committee on November 24, 2026 amended a special performance-based restricted stock unit grant to Chief Executive Officer Josh Weinstein originally made on August 22, 2022. The amendment shortens the performance period to end November 30, 2026 instead of November 30, 2027, reduces the maximum payout from 200% to 180% of the 500,000 target units, and adds a two-year post-vesting holding requirement and enhanced clawback provisions.

items.title: Skydance Corp terminates $4 billion securitization facility and redeems debt notes
items.summary: Skydance Corp's subsidiary WBD Receivables terminated its $4 billion securitization facility on November 20, 2026, as part of the company's capital plan. The company also delivered redemption notices for three series of notes due in 2027: $584.3 million of 2.90% Senior Notes, $33.4 million of 3.80% Notes, and €84.3 million of 1.90% Senior Notes, all to be redeemed at par plus accrued interest.

items.summary: Raymond James Financial disclosed October 2026 operating metrics showing client assets under administration of $1.95 trillion, up 11% year-over-year and 1% from September 2026. Private Client Group assets in fee-based accounts rose 14% year-over-year to $1.17 trillion, while financial assets under management grew 25% year-over-year to $346.4 billion. The company cited strong advisor retention and recruiting, along with market appreciation and net asset inflows, as drivers of growth.
items.title: Raymond James Financial reports October 2026 operating data

items.summary: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026, up from 2.2 percent in the second quarter, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis second estimate. Growth was driven by increases in investment, consumer spending and government spending, partly offset by a decrease in exports and an increase in imports.
items.title: US GDP grew 4.3 percent in third quarter 2026

items.summary: Personal income increased $201.8 billion, or 0.7 percent at a monthly rate, in October 2026, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Disposable personal income rose $200.5 billion, or 0.8 percent, while personal consumption expenditures increased $63.8 billion, or 0.3 percent. The personal saving rate stood at 4.1 percent of disposable personal income.
items.title: Personal income rose 0.7 percent in October, consumption grew 0.3 percent

items.summary: Imperial Oil Limited announced the appointment of J.E. (Jim) Burgess, age 52, as senior vice-president, finance and administration, and controller effective March 1, 2027. Mr. Burgess, currently treasurer, succeeds D.E. (Dan) Lyons, who will retire after 36 years of service with Imperial Oil Limited and Exxon Mobil Corporation.
items.title: Imperial Oil appoints Jim Burgess as senior vice-president, finance and administration

items.summary: Deere & Company reported net income of $1.051 billion, or $3.89 per share, for the fourth quarter of 2026, down 1% from $1.065 billion, or $3.93 per share, in the prior-year quarter. For the full year 2026, net income was $4.860 billion, or $17.95 per share, down 3% from $5.027 billion, or $18.50 per share, in 2025. The company forecast net income for 2027 in the range of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, which includes an estimated one-time, non-cash pension settlement charge of $0.25 billion to $0.40 billion.
items.title: Deere reports $1.051 billion fourth-quarter net income, full-year $4.860 billion

items.summary: Alphabet Inc. closed an underwritten public offering of C$6 billion in Canadian dollar-denominated senior notes on November 24, 2026. The offering consists of four tranches: C$2 billion of 4.100% notes due 2029, C$1.25 billion of 4.800% notes due 2034, C$1.5 billion of 5.325% notes due 2038, and C$1.25 billion of 6.000% notes due 2066.
items.title: Alphabet closes C$6 billion Canadian dollar senior notes offering

items.summary: Restaurant Brands International completed a $1 billion public offering of senior secured notes on November 24, 2026: $500 million of 6.000% notes due 2031 and $500 million of 6.400% notes due 2036. The company used proceeds to repay a portion of outstanding borrowings under its term loan B facility and to pay fees and expenses related to the offering.
items.title: Restaurant Brands International completes $1B senior secured notes offering

items.summary: DTE Energy, DTE Electric and DTE Gas each amended their five-year credit agreements on November 18, 2026, extending the termination date by one year to October 22, 2031. DTE Electric increased its aggregate commitments from $1.0B to $1.25B. Following the amendments, aggregate commitments are $1.5B for DTE Energy, $1.25B for DTE Electric and $300M for DTE Gas.
items.title: DTE Energy extends credit facilities to 2031 and increases commitments
